title: Exact Directed-Torus DAG Obstructions, Universal All-n Partial-Transpose Indecomposability, and Fourier Collapse Thresholds for Tensor Powers of Generalized Choi Maps
abstract: Whether non-trivial tensor-stable positive (TSP) maps exist is a central open problem in quantum information theory closely connected to the existence of NPT bound entanglement. We establish three exact algebraic and combinatorial theorems governing arbitrary tensor powers Phi[a,b,c]^{otimes n} of the three-parameter generalized Choi family on M_3(C). First, we prove that for every a < 2 and b > 0, Phi[a,b,0] is never 2-positive (via an explicit rank-2 witness eliminating all b-dependence) and Phi[a,b,0]^{otimes n} is strictly partial-transpose indecomposable for every n >= 1 (cannot be written as sum_{S subset [n]} C_S o T_S with all C_S completely positive). Second, we prove a directed-torus DAG limit law on G_{3,n}: any acyclic support S subset Z_3^n isolates the b-independent principal submatrix M_S(a)_{uv} = (-1)^{d_H(u,v)} a^{n - d_H(u,v)} as b-shifts vanish along a topological scaling. An exhaustive 512-subset classification of G_{3,2} fixes the sharp 2-copy b -> +infty threshold at a_*(2) = 1.71298487..., the unique positive root of a^4 - 2a^3 + 2a^2 - 2a - 1 = 0, while explicit 8-vertex and 16-vertex DAGs push a_*(3) > 1.950079 and a_*(4) > 1.997061 (99.853% of the completely positive boundary a = 2); by contrast, the Boolean subcube Q_n reaches only a_*(Q_n) = 1. Third, an explicit rank-2 Fourier test family yields an exact 3-parameter n-copy necessary condition proving total 2-copy collapse for all a <= 1 and b > 0, a closed-form 2-copy threshold b_F(a), unconditional non-existence of TSP maps across the entire c = 0 indecomposable face with linear asymptotic slope 3(2-a)/(2 ln a), and exact 9x9 Eisenstein Q(omega) Hermitian LDL* refutations of 2-copy positivity for strictly interior (c > 0) indecomposable maps. All core identities are formally verified in Lean 4.36.0 (20 theorems, 0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice) alongside 16 zero-float SHA-256 certificates and 56 adversarial pytest checks.
